description: Reference vectors for the calculus: each vector names an entry function in a program, the argument values, and the value the reference evaluator produces. The evaluator is the truth (the calculus is self-referential), so a lowered target must reproduce these outputs bit for bit; the vectors pin lowering fidelity, not logic. Value encoding: one-key objects tag the type; 64-bit integers travel as decimal strings.

vectors.name: wrap_i8_add
vectors.program: fn f(a: i8) -> i8 = a + 1

vectors.name: wrap_u8_sub
vectors.program: fn f(a: u8) -> u8 = a - 1

vectors.name: trunc_div_negative_dividend
vectors.program: fn f(a: i64, b: i64) -> i64 = a / b

vectors.name: trunc_rem_sign_of_dividend
vectors.program: fn f(a: i64, b: i64) -> i64 = a % b

vectors.name: div_by_zero_is_total_zero
vectors.program: fn f(a: i64, b: i64) -> i64 = a / b

vectors.name: intmin_div_minus_one_wraps
vectors.program: fn f(a: i64, b: i64) -> i64 = a / b

vectors.name: unsigned_div_high_bit
vectors.program: fn f(a: u8, b: u8) -> u8 = a / b

vectors.name: to_int_truncates_toward_zero
vectors.program: fn f(x: float) -> i64 = to_int(x) ?? -1

vectors.name: to_float_lossy_above_2p53
vectors.program: fn f(a: i64) -> float = to_float(a)

vectors.name: concat_strings
vectors.program: fn f(a: string, b: string) -> string = a ++ b

vectors.name: short_circuit_and
vectors.program: fn f(a: i64) -> bool = let y = a in y > 0 && y < 10

vectors.name: map_filter_fold
vectors.program:
fn dbl(x: i64) -> i64 = x * 2
fn pos(x: i64) -> bool = x > 0
fn add(a: i64, x: i64) -> i64 = a + x
fn f(xs: []i64) -> i64 = fold(filter(map(xs, dbl), pos), 0, add)

vectors.name: list_builtins
vectors.program:
fn lt2(x: i64) -> bool = x < 2
fn f(xs: []i64) -> i64 = length(xs) + (head(xs) ?? 0) + (get(xs, 1) ?? 0) + (find(xs, lt2) ?? -1)

vectors.name: map_builtins
vectors.program: fn f(m: map[string]i64, k: string) -> i64 = get_or(m, k, 0) + (lookup(m, k) ?? 0)

vectors.name: match_known_arm
vectors.program: fn f(p: pm) -> string = match p { card(c) => "C" pix(x) => "P" Unknown(u) => u }

vectors.name: match_unknown_arm
vectors.program: fn f(p: pm) -> string = match p { card(c) => "C" pix(x) => "P" Unknown(u) => u }

vectors.name: optional_some
vectors.program: fn f(a: i64) -> i64? = if a > 0 then Some(a) else None

vectors.name: optional_none
vectors.program: fn f(a: i64) -> i64? = if a > 0 then Some(a) else None

vectors.name: struct_ctor
vectors.program: fn f() -> card = card { last4: "1234" }
